claims.text: The baseline is an as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu thin-film protective coating on a conventional metal substrate.
The baseline coating has a room-temperature-processed microstructure.
The intervention is pre-oxidation annealing at approximately 300°C in a mildly oxidizing atmosphere.
Pre-oxidation at approximately 300°C will form a uniform, adherent oxide layer on FeNiCrCoCu.
The oxide layer will passivate the FeNiCrCoCu surface and act as a barrier against further high-temperature oxidation.
The pre-formed oxide layer will stabilize grain boundaries.
The pre-formed oxide layer will limit thermally activated microstructural changes.
The pre-formed oxide scale will reduce direct metal-to-metal contact during sliding.
The pre-formed oxide scale will reduce mechanical degradation during high-temperature sliding.
Pre-oxidation will improve the high-temperature wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu coatings relative to untreated coatings.
Pre-oxidized coatings will have lower wear rates or wear depths than untreated coatings at approximately 500°C.
Pre-oxidized coatings will exhibit more stable friction coefficients than untreated coatings.
Pre-oxidized coatings will undergo less grain coarsening than untreated coatings during high-temperature wear.
Pre-oxidized coatings will exhibit less oxide-scale spalling than untreated coatings during high-temperature wear.
The proposed effect applies from room temperature to approximately 500°C under loads typical of high-temperature applications.
The effect may change substantially outside the stated temperature or loading regime.
The test compares pre-oxidized and untreated FeNiCrCoCu coatings under identical sliding conditions at 500°C and the same mechanical load.

Failure to obtain a statistically significant wear-resistance improvement, or observation of similar or higher wear, unstable friction, or premature oxide spallation, would falsify the stated composite hypothesis.
